text: If we are here, we can choose one of the possible channels that are three at two point four gigahertz, twelve at five gigahertz, twenty four and six gigahertz. So many more. And this matches the indeed evolution of the technology popularity, because WiFi has become more and more popular. So at the beginning, these three channels were enough. Now that we have access points everywhere, we needed to use more frequency channels. Why? Because in this way we can avoid interference. Consider this case: if you have two different access points, you may want to let one access point operate here. And the second access point operate here, so that they use different frequencies, so their transmissions are separated. Because they use different frequencies. So it's like one frequency channel is like one classroom. Two hundred and six, where we are. This other frequency channel is two hundred and four, the other classroom. This one is the other classroom, two hundred and two. So if there are three professors.
